events.address: 214 N Pokegama Ave, Grand Rapids, MN
events.description: Join us for an afternoon of live music, community, and celebration as we honor four families whose musical traditions have left a lasting mark on Grand Rapids: the LaPlant, Miltich, Downing, and Aultman families. Community Open House Jam Sunday, September 20, 2026 2:00 PM – 7:00 PM Rapids Brewing Co., Grand Rapids, MN Whether you’re a lifelong musician, an occasional picker, or simply someone who loves great music and local history, you’re invited to be part of this special gathering. Bring your instrument and join the open jam sessions or sit back and enjoy an afternoon filled with music, storytelling, and community spirit. Hosted by Kari Hedlund of KAXE, the event will also feature displays of historical family photographs and two ceremonial toasts at 3:00 PM and 5:30 PM celebrating the enduring contributions of these remarkable families to the cultural life of Grand Rapids. Food and beverages will be available for purchase from Rapids Brewing Company throughout the event. This is a celebration of legacy, friendship, and the power of music to bring people together across generations. Everyone is welcome! Admission is free. events.title: Organ concert: From Baroque to Classical Brilliance
events.address: 201 West 4th Street, Duluth, MN
events.description: The Friends of the Felgemaker proudly present “From Baroque to Classical Brilliance.” This event will be a grand afternoon of classical masterpieces featuring the historic Felgemaker pipe organ and an intimate chamber orchestra. The concert showcases magnificent works by three legendary 18th Century composers: George Frideric Handel, Joseph Haydn, and Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart. Performing the music will be Sacred Heart Music Center’s Resident Organist, Dr. Charles Sundquist, who will be joined by some of the region’s finest orchestral players: Laurie Bastian and Kristin Sande, violin; Kevin Hoeschen, viola; Byron Klimek, cello; Brett Linski and Madeline Miller, oboe; and Tom Pfotenhauer and Stacy Carolan, on trumpet. Come hear this chamber music program combining the thrilling power of the Felgemaker pipe organ with the grace of a chamber orchestra in Sacred Heart Music Center’s renowned acoustical space. events.description: Legendary Swedish group Jaerv and Twin Cities-based duo OK Factor return to the beautiful Sacred Heart alter stage Friday, Oct. 16. The group offers a varied stage performance where five-voiced tunes blend in with energetic dances and free improvisations. events.title: Silent Film: The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari
events.address: 201 West 4th Street, Duluth, MN
events.description: Organist Aaron David Miller accompanies the classic 1920 silent horror film “The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari.” The Friends of The Felgemaker invite you to experience what it was like to attend a silent movie! Renowned organist Aaron David Miller will accompany the silent film “The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari” at 7 p.m. Friday, Oct. 23 on the historic Felgemaker pipe organ housed at Sacred Heart Music Center. “The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari” is a groundbreaking German horror film which set standards for creative camera work and featured a dark and twisted style of storytelling. He has won numerous international awards for improvisation and has given concerts and accompanied silent films across the country. events.title: Mason Jennings
events.address: 201 West 4th Street, Duluth, MN
events.description: Minnesota troubadour Mason Jennings returns performing old favorites and work from his new album “Dark Wings.” “I love song craft,” says Mason Jennings, a folksinger who has spent over two decades honing his craft both on stage and in the studio. “A song is like a boat on the water, and you’re trying to make it float with as few pieces as possible. If you do it right, a song can be very healing.” For Jennings, songwriting has always been about a personal connection, both with his audience and himself. He’s known for an unpretentious, emotive approach to folk music, combining introspective lyrics with acoustic melodies. His work has drawn comparisons to genre greats, including Nick Drake, John Fahey, and Tom Waits. But Jennings’ sound is distinctly his own, one that blends vulnerability with strength, simplicity with complexity. That style comes through on his new record: “Dark Wings.” His 18th studio album, the record finds Jennings moving between raw honesty about childhood scars, dark thoughts, spiritual questioning and a stubborn belief in the power of love. Duluth-based singer-songwriter and bandleader Breanne Marie of Breanne Marie & The Front Porch Sinners will open with a solo set. Advance E-tickets are available for $25 (plus $3.52 in fees) on Eventbrite HERE. Paper tickets will be available for $25 at Zenith Bookstore in West Duluth (plus $1 handling fee) and at Globe News in Superior (cash only). Tickets will be available at the door for $30 while supply lasts. Doors at 6:30. Music at 7:30.
